architecture.note: Heirloom Room on PC prefers OpenXR (Meta, SteamVR, Pico Streaming XR, or Sony via SteamVR). The browser viewer uses WebXR, which on a Windows PC is usually backed by the active OpenXR runtime. Quest browser and Cardboard skip the PC runtime and sit in WebXR directly.

legal.copy: Heirloom never ships Meta, Sony, Pico, or Steam installers, and never links to cracked Virtual Desktop. Downloads below are official vendor or open-source releases only. Virtual Desktop is optional paid polish — skip it unless you already own it.

A.label: First-class
A.blurb: Official free PC path. OpenXR or WebXR works with vendor software.

B.label: Official but fiddly
B.blurb: Vendor software is free; hardware or an experimental runtime may be required.

C.label: Guided workaround
C.blurb: Community or browser paths. Expect extra steps and lower fidelity.

meta_horizon_link.name: Meta Horizon Link
meta_horizon_link.notes: Windows only. One installer covers USB Link and wireless Air Link.

steam.name: Steam
steam.notes: Needed for SteamVR, the PSVR2 App, and most OpenXR PC titles.

steamvr.name: SteamVR
steamvr.notes: Set SteamVR as the OpenXR runtime: SteamVR → Settings → OpenXR.

alvr.name: ALVR
alvr.notes: Free wireless SteamVR streamer. PC host is Windows or Linux — not macOS. Match streamer and headset app versions.

sidequest.name: SideQuest
sidequest.notes: Sideload ALVR on Pico and on Quest 1 (Quest 2/3/Pro can use the Meta store app).

pico_connect.name: PICO Connect
pico_connect.notes: Free streaming for Pico OS 5.11.2+. Experimental OpenXR: run add_runtime.bat as Administrator inside the PICO Connect folder, then confirm PicoStreamingXR is the active runtime.

psvr2_app.name: PlayStation VR2 App
psvr2_app.notes: Free on Steam. Does not replace the paid Sony PC adapter. Not ALVR.

openxr.name: OpenXR
openxr.notes: The PC API Heirloom prefers. Only one active runtime at a time (Meta, SteamVR, PicoStreamingXR, or Monado).

webxr.name: WebXR
webxr.notes: Browser path. Works in Quest Browser and on a PC when an OpenXR runtime is installed. Needs HTTPS or localhost.

oasis.name: Oasis Driver for Windows Mixed Reality
oasis.notes: Community SteamVR driver for Reverb / Odyssey / Explorer after Microsoft removed WMR in Windows 11 24H2. Fragile. NVIDIA or AMD RDNA; no Intel GPU.

monado.name: Monado
monado.notes: Linux OpenXR runtime. Pair with ALVR's experimental Android/Monado client.

virtual_desktop.name: Virtual Desktop
virtual_desktop.notes: Paid wireless polish with its own OpenXR runtime (VDXR). Optional. Never required. Do not use cracked copies.

baseline: Windows 10 22H2 or later for most PCVR. SteamVR also runs on Linux; Meta Link does not.
Dedicated GPU: NVIDIA GTX 1060 6GB / AMD RX 480 class or better for wireless streaming.
USB 3.0+ Type-A or USB-C 3.2 (5 Gb/s) for wired Quest Link. Avoid unpowered hubs.
For wireless: wire the PC to the router. Put the headset on 5 GHz or 6 GHz, same LAN, not a guest SSID.
8 GB RAM minimum; 16 GB is the comfortable floor.
psvr2: Sony PlayStation VR2 PC adapter (paid hardware, CFI-ZVP1) — required. Software is free.
DisplayPort 1.4 straight into the GPU. No USB-C DisplayPort, no HDMI converters, no DP hubs.
USB 3.0 Type-A directly on the PC (not a hub or extension).
Bluetooth for Sense controllers. Buy a compatible USB Bluetooth adapter if the board has none.
See Sony's PC spec page before you buy the adapter.

wifi_tips: Same subnet as the PC. Guest / AP isolation / client isolation will fail discovery.
Prefer 5 GHz or Wi-Fi 6/6E. 2.4 GHz is a last resort.
Sit near the router. Walls and microwave ovens wreck Air Link and ALVR.
Ethernet the PC. Do not stream PC-to-headset over the same wireless hop twice.
Disable Wi-Fi power saving on the adapter. Pause VPN while streaming.
If Air Link stutters, drop to a wired Link cable or try ALVR with HEVC on a wired PC.
openxr_notes: Only one OpenXR runtime can be active. Switching vendors without resetting this is the usual 'headset not found' cause.
Windows stores the active runtime at %LOCALAPPDATA%\openxr\1\active_runtime.json. Linux uses /etc/xdg/openxr/1/ or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/openxr/1/, overridable with OPENXR_RUNTIME_JSON.
SteamVR: Settings → OpenXR → Set SteamVR as OpenXR Runtime.
Meta: install Horizon Link, then let it register the Meta OpenXR runtime (or pick it in the Link app).
Pico: PICO Connect folder → add_runtime.bat as Administrator → PicoStreamingXR. To undo, set SteamVR as OpenXR runtime again.
Restart the browser after changing the runtime. Chrome/Edge WebXR reads it at launch.
Native WinUI Room viewer (OpenXR directly) is still deferred. Until then, Sit uses WebXR on top of that runtime.

fix_openxr.label: Use HTTPS or localhost
fix_openxr.detail: WebXR only starts in a secure context. Open the studio on https:// or http://localhost, not a LAN HTTP IP.

fix_openxr.label: Browser exposes WebXR
fix_openxr.detail: Chrome, Edge, or Quest Browser. Firefox needs the WebXR flag and is a poor PC VR host.

fix_openxr.label: immersive-vr is supported
fix_openxr.detail: Headset awake, steamvr/link/pico/psvr2 app running. If this is false on a PC, the OpenXR runtime is missing or not active.

fix_openxr.label: Active OpenXR runtime file
fix_openxr.detail: Confirm active_runtime.json points at SteamVR, Meta, PicoStreamingXR, or Monado — not a stale WMR package.

fix_openxr.label: One runtime at a time
fix_openxr.detail: If you ran Pico add_runtime.bat and also use SteamVR, pick one. SteamVR → OpenXR is the safe reset.

fix_openxr.label: Restart the browser after switching
fix_openxr.detail: WebXR caches the runtime. Fully quit Chrome/Edge, then put the headset on again.

headsets.name: Meta Quest 2 / 3 / 3S / Pro
headsets.pain: Air Link needs a clean 5 GHz/6 GHz LAN. Cheap USB-C cables fail Link. Developer Mode is only needed for SideQuest, not for Link.

headsets.name: Valve Index
headsets.pain: Needs SteamVR, DisplayPort, and lighthouses powered. Set SteamVR as the OpenXR runtime.

headsets.name: HTC Vive / Vive Pro (Index-class SteamVR)
headsets.pain: Same SteamVR + OpenXR path as Index. USB + DisplayPort + base stations.

headsets.name: Windows Mixed Reality (Reverb, Odyssey, Explorer)
headsets.pain: Microsoft removed Mixed Reality Portal in Windows 11 24H2. Official WMR-for-SteamVR is deprecated and fragile. Community Oasis driver is the current path — NVIDIA/AMD only.

headsets.name: Pico Neo 3 / 4 / 4 Ultra
headsets.pain: PICO Connect is free but fiddly. Experimental OpenXR needs add_runtime.bat as Administrator. ALVR on Pico is a SideQuest sideload.

headsets.name: PlayStation VR2 (PC adapter)
headsets.pain: Not ALVR. Requires Sony's paid PC adapter plus a DisplayPort 1.4 GPU output and Bluetooth for Sense. Software (SteamVR + PSVR2 App) is free.

headsets.name: ALVR others (Vive Focus, YVR, PhoneVR, Android/Monado)
headsets.pain: Free, but you install the matching ALVR client (SideQuest or vendor store) and keep SteamVR running on the PC. Android/Monado is experimental.

headsets.name: Apple Vision Pro
headsets.pain: ALVR has an App Store client. The PC streamer is Windows or Linux — macOS host is unsupported. Use a Windows PC on the same LAN. Safari WebXR is limited.
headsets.host_note: macOS cannot host ALVR. Pair Vision Pro with a Windows (or Linux) PC.

headsets.name: Smartphone Cardboard / browser WebXR
headsets.pain: Lowest-fidelity room sit. Open this studio in the phone browser, tap Enter in VR, drop the phone in a Cardboard viewer. No SteamVR, no OpenXR runtime.

meta_link.label: Meta Quest Link (USB)
meta_link.blurb: Official wired path. USB-C 3.2 cable into the PC, Horizon Link running, OpenXR via the Meta runtime.

air_link.label: Air Link (Wi-Fi)
air_link.blurb: Official wireless path. Same Horizon Link app. 5 GHz or 6 GHz, PC on Ethernet.

webxr.label: WebXR in the browser
webxr.blurb: Simplest path. Quest Browser, or Chrome/Edge on a PC that already has an OpenXR runtime. Heirloom Sit uses this today.

openxr.label: Native OpenXR runtime
openxr.blurb: Preferred PC API. SteamVR, Meta Link, PicoStreamingXR, or Monado registers as the active runtime. WebXR on Chrome/Edge rides on top of it.

steamvr.label: SteamVR (+ OpenXR bridge)
steamvr.blurb: Index, Vive, and anything ALVR/Pico/PSVR2 already presents to SteamVR. Turn on the OpenXR bridge in SteamVR settings.

alvr.label: ALVR (free wireless)
alvr.blurb: Open-source SteamVR streamer. Quest store app, or SideQuest APK for Pico / Quest 1. Windows or Linux host — not Mac.

pico_connect.label: PICO Connect
pico_connect.blurb: Official free Pico streaming. Install the Windows (or Mac desktop-view) app and the headset Connect title.

pico_openxr.label: Pico experimental OpenXR (add_runtime.bat)
pico_openxr.blurb: Inside the PICO Connect install, run add_runtime.bat as Administrator so PicoStreamingXR is the active OpenXR runtime. Experimental. Reset via SteamVR → OpenXR if it breaks other headsets.

psvr2_adapter.label: PSVR2 PC adapter + Steam app
psvr2_adapter.blurb: Paid Sony adapter + free PlayStation VR2 App on Steam + SteamVR. DisplayPort 1.4 and Bluetooth. Not ALVR.

oasis.label: Oasis (community WMR → SteamVR)
oasis.blurb: Community SteamVR driver after Microsoft removed WMR. Official WMR-for-SteamVR is deprecated. Treat as fragile.

virtual_desktop.label: Virtual Desktop (paid, optional)
virtual_desktop.blurb: Optional polish. Buy it from the official store if you want VDXR. Heirloom never requires it and will not link to cracks.

meta_link.title: Install Horizon Link on the PC
meta_link.body: Download the official Meta Horizon Link app for Windows. No other 'Oculus cracked' installer.

meta_link.title: Use a real USB 3 cable
meta_link.body: USB-C 3.2, 5 Gb/s or faster. Charge-only cables fail silently. Plug into the PC, not a monitor hub.

meta_link.title: Put the headset on Link
meta_link.body: Headset Settings → System → Quest Link → enable, then Launch Quest Link. Confirm the PC name.

meta_link.title: OpenXR runtime
meta_link.body: Let Link register the Meta OpenXR runtime, or set SteamVR as OpenXR if you prefer that bridge.

meta_link.title: Sit in the room
meta_link.body: In Chrome/Edge on the PC, open Heirloom → Rooms → Sit → Enter in VR. Or open this page in Quest Browser for the simple WebXR path.

air_link.title: Same Horizon Link app
air_link.body: Air Link is built into Meta Horizon Link. Do not buy a third-party 'air link' APK.

air_link.title: Wire the PC, 5 GHz for the headset
air_link.body: Ethernet the PC to the router. Headset on 5 GHz or 6 GHz, same LAN, not guest Wi-Fi.

air_link.title: Pair Air Link
air_link.body: In the headset: Quest Link → Air Link → select the PC. Allow the prompt on the PC.

air_link.title: Enter in VR
air_link.body: Once Air Link shows the PC dashboard, open Heirloom Sit in the browser on the PC and press Enter in VR.

webxr.title: Open a supported browser
webxr.body: Quest Browser on the headset, or Chrome/Edge on a PC that already has SteamVR/Link/Pico/PSVR2 running.

webxr.title: Stay on HTTPS
webxr.body: WebXR refuses plain HTTP on a LAN IP. Use https:// or http://localhost.

webxr.title: Tap Enter in VR
webxr.body: Allow the immersive session. Seated tracking is enough for a Heirloom Room sit.

steamvr.title: Install Steam and SteamVR
steamvr.body: Both are free. SteamVR is the host for Index, Vive, ALVR, Pico Connect, and PSVR2.

steamvr.title: Set the OpenXR runtime
steamvr.body: SteamVR → Settings → OpenXR → Set SteamVR as OpenXR Runtime. Restart the browser.

steamvr.title: Headset ready in SteamVR
steamvr.body: Status should be standing / seated, not 'headset not detected'. Then Enter in VR from Sit.

openxr.title: Pick one runtime
openxr.body: Meta Link, SteamVR, PicoStreamingXR, or Monado — not several at once.

openxr.title: Confirm active_runtime.json
openxr.body: Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\openxr\1\active_runtime.json. Use the in-app Fix OpenXR check.

openxr.title: Browser on top
openxr.body: Chrome/Edge WebXR uses that runtime. Restart the browser after switching.

alvr.title: SteamVR on the PC
alvr.body: ALVR is a SteamVR plugin. Install SteamVR first (Windows or Linux, not macOS).

alvr.title: ALVR streamer from GitHub
alvr.body: Download the official ALVR release (Launcher). Never a random 'ALVR full cracked' zip.

alvr.title: Headset client
alvr.body: Quest 2/3/Pro: Meta store ALVR app. Pico / Quest 1 / Focus / YVR: SideQuest sideload of the matching APK. Match versions.

alvr.title: Same Wi-Fi, then trust
alvr.body: PC on Ethernet. Headset on 5 GHz. Accept the client in the ALVR streamer, then Enter in VR from Heirloom Sit.

pico_connect.title: PICO Connect on the PC
pico_connect.body: Official download from picoxr.com — Windows 10 22H2+. Headset OS 5.11.2+.

pico_connect.title: Connect app on the headset
pico_connect.body: Install PICO Connect from the Pico store. Pair over Wi-Fi or USB 3.

pico_connect.title: SteamVR if you need OpenXR via Steam
pico_connect.body: PICO Connect can present the headset to SteamVR. Then set SteamVR as the OpenXR runtime.

pico_openxr.title: Install PICO Connect first
pico_openxr.body: The experimental runtime lives inside that install.

pico_openxr.title: Run add_runtime.bat as Administrator
pico_openxr.body: Search under C:\Program Files\PICO Connect\ for add_runtime.bat. This registers PicoStreamingXR.

pico_openxr.title: Know how to undo it
pico_openxr.body: If Index/Quest/SteamVR break, SteamVR → Settings → OpenXR → Set SteamVR as OpenXR Runtime.

psvr2_adapter.title: You need the Sony PC adapter
psvr2_adapter.body: CFI-ZVP1, paid hardware. There is no ALVR path for PSVR2. Software is free; the adapter is not.

psvr2_adapter.title: Free apps on Steam
psvr2_adapter.body: Install Steam, then SteamVR, then the PlayStation VR2 App. Keep the PSVR2 App installed after setup — firmware lives there.

psvr2_adapter.title: Cables: DP 1.4 + USB 3 + power
psvr2_adapter.body: Adapter USB-A 3.0 into the PC (no hub). DisplayPort 1.4 into the GPU (no USB-C DP, no HDMI dongle). Power the adapter, then the headset.

psvr2_adapter.title: Bluetooth for Sense
psvr2_adapter.body: Pair Sense controllers over Bluetooth. If the PC has no radio, Sony lists compatible USB adapters. Built-in Intel BT is often fine; cheap dongles are not.

psvr2_adapter.title: Finish in the PSVR2 App
psvr2_adapter.body: Open the Steam app, complete play area and firmware. SteamVR should see the headset. Then Heirloom Sit → Enter in VR.

oasis.title: Know that official WMR is gone
oasis.body: Windows 11 24H2 removed Mixed Reality Portal and WMR for SteamVR. Do not hunt for old Microsoft Store packages.

oasis.title: Oasis community driver (free on Steam)
oasis.body: Install SteamVR, then Oasis Driver for Windows Mixed Reality. NVIDIA or AMD RDNA. No Intel GPU. Read the wiki first.

oasis.title: OpenXR via SteamVR
oasis.body: Set SteamVR as the OpenXR runtime. Expect this path to stay fragile.

virtual_desktop.title: Buy it if you want polish
virtual_desktop.body: Official site or Steam. Optional. Heirloom works without it.

virtual_desktop.title: Never a crack
virtual_desktop.body: Cracked Virtual Desktop is malware territory and a ToS violation. Skip this path if you do not own it — use Link, Air Link, ALVR, or Pico Connect instead.
